title: Slot segmentation and KV watermarking for mixed-length continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Mixed prompt/response length workloads (chatty agents + long context prompts) cause the continuous batcher to create wide length dispersion inside slots. This leads to: 1) high token tail latency for short requests pinned behind long ones, 2) KV cache fragmentation and underutilized slabs, and 3) uneven GPU memory pressure causing occasional OOMs on multi-tenant Dedicated nodes.

Objective: Tune the continuous batching scheduler by introducing slot segmentation (short/medium/long bands) and a KV watermarking policy that proactively trims low-value KV shards during slot transitions. Goal is to reduce 95th/99th percentile token latency for short requests on mixed workloads while lowering peak GPU memory by at least 20% under a representative production trace.

Scope: Implementation touches the scheduler (slot classification, admission), KV cache manager (watermarks, async reclamation hooks), and the runtime evictor (GPU slab rebalancer). This ticket includes design, prototype, benchmarks, canary rollout, and monitoring dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: p95 token generation latency for short requests (<=64 tokens) improves by >=15% on mixed trace compared to baseline v2.1
peak GPU memory usage under mixed workload reduced by >=20% on Dedicated small (4xA10) instance shape
KV cache fragmentation metric (free slab ratio variance) reduced by >=25% across slots
No increase in median latency for long requests (>=1024 tokens) beyond 5%
Canary running for 72 hours with <0.1% error rate uplift and roll-forward plan verified
tasks: Design doc: slot segmentation thresholds + KV watermark algorithm (prototype)
Implement slot classifier in batcher (short/med/long bands, dynamic thresholds)
KV manager: implement watermark levels and async reclaim hook tied to slot handoff
Runtime: add GPU slab rebalancer to prefer contiguous slabs for active slots
Instrument: per-slot latency, kv-frag, slab-usage, and per-token cost metrics
Benchmark: run 3 trace mixes (chat-heavy, prompt-heavy, uniform) across shapes
Canary: staged deploy to 5% traffic, monitor dashboards and rollback criteria
Docs & runbook: update console runbooks and release notes

links: Related ticket ENG-47683: observability dashboard wiring
risks: Aggressive KV reclaiming could increase tail latency for long-running generation if we evict useful KV pages during active decode
Slot misclassification under rapidly varying sequence-length distributions could starve a band and cause jitter
GPU slab rebalancer may interact poorly with other reclamation (OS-level CUDA memory manager) on some driver versions
open_questions: Should thresholds be static percentiles (p10/p50/p90) per tenant or use cluster-wide adaptive thresholds?
What is the safe minimum hot-resident percentage of KV pages we should preserve for long requests to avoid rehydration cost?
Do we need tenant-specific policies (high-SLA customers pinned to less-aggressive reclaim) and how to express in routing config?
deliverables: Merged scheduler + kv-manager changes in runtime repo
Perf report with production-trace benchmarks and parameter sweeps
